statement: The oldest fossils confidently placed on the Neanderthal branch (post-dating the split from the modern-human lineage but pre-dating classic Neanderthal morphology) are from Sima de los Huesos, Atapuerca, Spain, dated to approximately 430,000 years ago via uranium-series and paleomagnetic methods, with nuclear DNA confirming their placement on the Neanderthal lineage.

sources.citation: Arsuaga, J.L. et al. "Neandertal roots: Cranial and chronological evidence from Sima de los Huesos." Science 344: 1358-1363.
sources.author: Arsuaga et al.

sources.citation: Meyer, M. et al. "Nuclear DNA sequences from the Middle Pleistocene Sima de los Huesos hominins." Nature 531: 504-507.
sources.author: Meyer et al.

does_not_demonstrate: that these individuals were "Neanderthals" in the strict classic morphological sense — they are proto-Neanderthal lineage material
